passages.provision_quote: human trafficking of a minor, in violation of subdivision (c) of Section 236.1, except, with respect to a violation of paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of Section 236.1, where the person who committed the offense was a victim of human trafficking, as described in subdivision (b) or (c) of Section 236.1, at the time of the offense;
passages.note: Author of a narrow bill adding one crime (human trafficking of a minor) to the serious-felony/Three Strikes list; shows a toughening direction but does not separate rung 4 from rung 5 across lawbreaking generally.

rows.reasoning: Grove authored SB 14, which adds human trafficking of a minor to the Penal Code's 'serious felony' definition so it triggers Three Strikes enhancements. This is a single, narrow crime-specific sentencing enhancement; it shows she favors harsher consequences for this offense but does not establish whether she holds the general 'real consequences, accountability is the priority' stance (rung 4) or 'impose the toughest penalties the law allows' (rung 5) across lawbreaking broadly, so it is broader than the instrument supports.
